rules.rule: Do not comment on code formatting: whitespace, indentation, line length, quote style, semicolons, or trailing commas. Prettier owns all of it (printWidth 120, single quotes, ES5 trailing commas, 2-space indent, semicolons) and eslint-config-prettier enforces it, so such comments can never be actionable. Naming conventions and structural consistency are still fair game.

Do not report violations of rules that eslint.config.mjs deliberately disables or relaxes. `@typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion` is off by design, `no-undef` is off, `no-constant-condition` does not check loops, and unused function parameters prefixed with an underscore are intentional. Check eslint.config.mjs before claiming a lint violation.
Do not request docstrings or JSDoc comments. This codebase does not use them as a convention, so the request is never actionable.
Do not suggest adding tests for a workspace that has no test harness. Most workspaces in this repository have none, and standing up a harness is out of scope for a typical change.

In Vue single-file components, flag reactivity bugs: losing reactivity by destructuring a reactive object, a missing `.value` on a ref, computed properties with side effects, a watcher that should be a computed, `v-for` without a stable `:key`, and props mutated directly instead of emitting.
Event listeners, intervals, timeouts, and observers registered in `onMounted` must be torn down in `onUnmounted`. These are long-lived single-page apps, so a leak accumulates across navigation.
Flag unchecked errors and ignored `err` returns. Much of the Go code regenerates committed JSON data files, so a write that fails partway can leave a truncated data file committed to the repository.
